title: Contract evolution and consumer safeguard playbook for runtime
creator: Ava Thompson
description: Define an operationally-safe, developer-friendly semantic versioning and deprecation policy for the Redwood serving runtime that covers network APIs (REST/gRPC), public SDK contracts, on-disk artifacts (saved sessions, cache formats), and control-plane rollouts. Deliver: (1) a written policy usable by engineers and PMs; (2) rollout gate definitions and automation templates; (3) a small set of upgrade tooling for preflight compatibility checks and automated migrations.
background: The serving runtime has expanded interfaces (HTTP/gRPC, CLI, saved session formats, on-disk KV layout) and third-party integrations. Historically we have handled compatibility case-by-case. As customers adopt pinned versions and private deployments, unpredictable breaking changes cause outages and expensive rollbacks. We need a reproducible contract evolution process that preserves safety for hosted, dedicated, and private installs while allowing reasonable progress.
proposal: Adopt a single semantic versioning baseline for the runtime codebase (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) combined with a compatibility taxonomy that maps change classes to version bumps and rollout requirements. Provide explicit deprecation headers, migration windows per artifact type, a formal LTS channel with defined maintenance windows, and two small tools: 'redwood-compat' (preflight checker) and 'redwood-migrate' (session/format transformer).
versioning_rules:
- MAJOR: required for incompatible changes to public network APIs (protocol, wire format) or on-disk artifacts that cannot be automatically migrated; also used when removing a deprecated endpoint before its expiry.
- MINOR: allowed for additive, backward-compatible features and changes that require client opt-in (new query parameters, non-breaking API additions).
- PATCH: bug fixes and internal non-behavioral changes.
- Compatibility taxon: Class A (breaking), Class B (soft-deprecations with auto-warn), Class C (non-breaking additions). Class A always triggers MAJOR, Class B tracked with warnings then MINOR when opt-in removed, Class C uses PATCH/MINOR as appropriate.
deprecation_policy:
- Deprecation must be announced in two places: server response header 'X-Redwood-Deprecation' and the public changelog entry.
- Default deprecation windows: hosted API endpoints: 90 days; SDK-visible surface changes: 6 months; on-disk/session formats or cache layout: 12 months (longer for private deployments).
- Deprecation metadata: each deprecated item must include 'replacement', 'removal_date', and migration guidance in our docs.
- If customers opt into extended support, document the SLA and process in the enterprise contract.
lts_channel_policy:
- LTS channel: runtime-LTS releases are produced from a stable minor (e.g., 2.8.x) and receive critical fixes and security patches only for 18 months.
- Security-only backports are allowed on LTS; non-security breaking fixes must follow full version cycle on non-LTS.
- We will publish the LTS schedule annually and provide upgrade tooling for LTS->nonLTS transitions.
- LTS releases are accompanied by a compatibility matrix and explicit migration recipes.
rollout_gates:
- Canary: 1% traffic to a canary pool for 24 hours with automatic health checks.
- Metrics gating: no more than +5% relative error rate, p99 latency regression < 15% relative, no increase in GPU OOMs greater than 0.5% absolute.
- Telemetry checks: model output quality regressions measured against golden prompts using automatic evals; alert if regression > 1.5% in any critical prompt set.
- Manual approval: any change touching on-disk formats or public SDKs requires product and release-engineering signoff before ramp.
- Rollback: automatic rollback trigger if any gate fails; documented rollback runbook for manual intervention.
upgrade_tooling:
- redwood-compat: CLI that analyzes running clusters, saved sessions, config files, and client SDK versions and emits a compatibility report and suggested remediation steps.
- redwood-migrate: transformers that convert old saved-session and KV cache formats to the new format using safe, idempotent operations with progress resume support.
- preflight behavior: CI-integrated compat-check that runs on PRs and release branches; fails builds when a public API change is detected without a deprecation PR.
- developer ergonomics: SDKs return explicit version negotiation errors with helpful messages and a link to migration docs.
migration_plan:
- Stage 0: publish policy and compatibility matrix; instrument the runtime to emit deprecation headers and compatibility signals.
- Stage 1: ship redwood-compat and integrate into CI and release pipeline (beta).
- Stage 2: ship redwood-migrate for one artifact type (saved sessions).
- Stage 3: run canary migrations on internal datasets and a subset of willing customers; gather feedback and iterate.
- Stage 4: enforce deprecation windows and require migration tooling in any MAJOR bump PR.
- Timing: goal to reach Stage 2 within 3 months of policy signoff.
testing_and_signoff:
- CI: compatibility tests added to the release pipeline covering REST/gRPC surface, saved session read/write matrix, SDK major/minor combos.
- E2E: golden prompt regression evaluation for each candidate release; threshold defined in rollout_gates.
- Manual review: PM and security signoff required for Class A or on-disk artifact changes; release engineering must approve rollout plan with gate thresholds.
- Acceptance: successful canary for two consecutive releases and migration tool tested on at least 3 real customer datasets.
acceptance_criteria:
- Policy document published and linked from contrib/release docs.
- redwood-compat CLI available in release pipeline and passes compatibility checks on the runtime-2.0 branch.
- redwood-migrate v0.1 migrates saved-session format with a documented rollback path.
- Automations for deprecation header injection and changelog generation are merged.
- At least one internal non-trivial upgrade completed with zero customer-visible downtime.
risks_mitigation:
- Risk: Customers with pinned private deployments will be unable to adopt breaking changes quickly. Mitigation: provide extended support paths, clear migration scripts, and priority migration engineering for enterprise customers.
- Risk: Migration tool failure causing data loss. Mitigation: tools are idempotent, operate in copy-on-write mode by default, and include a verification step before cutover.
- Risk: SDK ecosystem fragmentation. Mitigation: publish client compatibility tables and provide automated CI badges for major SDK repos.
notes:
This playbook emphasizes operational safety and developer empathy. We balance forward progress with practical migration windows, prioritizing on-disk and protocol changes for longer deprecation windows. The goal is predictable evolution rather than immediate freeze.
Key stakeholders: Runtime PlatEng, Release Engineering, SDK teams, Security, Product.
